sections.h2: Where is Fitchburg and how big is it?
sections.html:
Fitchburg is a city in northern Worcester County and the county's third-largest, with 41,946 residents at the 2020 census. It covers 28.1 square miles, almost all of it land, and sits at about 469 feet above sea level.

The Nashua River drains the city. Brown Hill, in the northwest corner, rises to 1,210 feet. Neighbors are Ashby to the north, Lunenburg to the east, Leominster to the south, Westminster to the west and a small piece of Ashburnham to the northwest.

sections.h2: What are the main Fitchburg neighborhoods?
sections.html:
Wikipedia lists a number of named areas, and a house's location inside them affects how it sells.

  • Downtown Fitchburg, Upper Common and Prichard-Pleasant Street
  • East Side, North Fitchburg, South Fitchburg and West Fitchburg
  • Cleghorn, Crockerville and The Patch
  • College Area, near Fitchburg State University
  • Green Acres Village, Tar Hill and Waite's Corner

The College Area sits near Fitchburg State University. Wikipedia notes the city is known for Victorian architecture built at the height of its mill-town prosperity, and a house of that age can carry older systems and repair needs.

sections.h2: What is the history of Fitchburg?
sections.html:
Europeans settled the area in 1730 as part of Lunenburg, and Fitchburg was incorporated in 1764 and became a city in 1872. It was named for John Fitch.

The Fitchburg Railroad ran through the Hoosac Tunnel to link Boston and Albany, and the rock drill used to build the tunnel was made in Fitchburg. Water-powered mills made machines, tools, clothing, paper and firearms. Paper mills lined the Nashua River, and the 1922 New England textile strike shut the mills over an attempted wage cut.

Fitchburg is also a shire town, so it hosts the Northern Worcester County Registry of Deeds, established in 1903. Deeds for Fitchburg property are recorded there.

Fitchburg's population grew steadily to about 43,000 by 1970, dropped to 39,580 in 1980, and has recovered since. The 2020 census counted 41,946, and the 2024 estimate is 42,145.

sections.h2: What does the Fitchburg economy look like?
sections.html:
The paper industry once employed a large share of residents. Today the city mixes manufacturing, education and health care.

The former Central Steam Plant, built in 1928 for the paper mills, was designated an EPA brownfield in 2008 and has been razed. Properties near old mill sites may involve environmental history, and buyers sometimes ask.

sections.h2: How do people get around Fitchburg?
sections.html:
The Montachusett Regional Transit Authority runs fixed-route buses, and it connects to the MBTA commuter rail at Fitchburg Station and Wachusett Station. Fitchburg Station is the second-to-last stop on the Fitchburg Line from North Station in Boston, and Wachusett is the last.

Fitchburg Municipal Airport occupies 335 acres near the Leominster line. The commuter line makes Fitchburg a possible home for people working in the Boston area.

sections.h2: What schools, parks and public services does Fitchburg have?
sections.html:
Fitchburg's public schools include Fitchburg High School, Goodrich Academy, Memorial Middle School and Longsjo Middle School, along with Crocker, South Street, Reingold and McKay elementary schools. Montachusett Regional Vocational Technical School, known as Monty Tech, also serves the area.

  • Coggshall Park, a 300-acre park established in 1894 with trails and access to Mirror Lake
  • Flat Rock Wild Life Sanctuary, 326 acres
  • Coolidge Park, with ball fields, a pool and a dog park
  • The Fitchburg Art Museum, founded in 1925

The fire department has 81 firefighters in three stations and answers about 12,000 calls a year. The police department covers 28 square miles and 192 miles of public road. Fitchburg Public Library was established in 1859.

sections.h2: What does winter mean for a Fitchburg house?
sections.html:
Fitchburg has a humid continental climate with cold, windy, snowy winters. The January average high is about 35 degrees Fahrenheit and the average low about 17, and July runs about 84 and 63.

That means heating cost, roof condition, ice dams and insulation are the first things buyers check. If your house has had a heating failure, a leaking roof or a burst pipe, sort out the repair cost before deciding between a listing and an as-is sale.

The 2020 census found a median age of 36.1 in Fitchburg. About 29.8 percent of the 16,143 households had children under 18, and 31.0 percent were one person living alone.

Hispanic or Latino residents of any race made up 30.1 percent of the population. Fitchburg State University and the city's rental stock give the market a mix of owner-occupants, investors and students, so a seller's best buyer depends on the house: a single-family home suits a household, while a multi-family building suits an investor who reads the rent roll closely.

sections.h2: What housing numbers apply to Fitchburg?
sections.html:
The 2020 census counted 17,452 housing units and 16,143 households in Fitchburg, with 7.5 percent of units vacant. The homeowner vacancy rate was 1.4 percent and the rental vacancy rate 5.3 percent.

The median age was 36.1. About 31 percent of households were one person. That mix of renters, investors and small owners means plenty of two- and three-family houses change hands in the city, and buyers of those look closely at rent rolls and repair needs.

sections.h2: What local rules should a Fitchburg seller ask about?
sections.html:
Rental rules, building permits, code enforcement and any open violations sit with the city.

It also helps to pull the permit history of the house. Work done without a permit, such as a finished basement or a converted attic, is the kind of thing a buyer's attorney will raise, and it is better to know the answer before you take an offer.

sections.h2: What does Massachusetts require when a Fitchburg house sells?
sections.html:
A smoke and carbon monoxide certificate of compliance from the Fitchburg fire department is required for a sale or transfer, and the state tells sellers to call as soon as the closing date is set. The department charges a fee.

The deed excise under chapter 64D applies as well, based on the price. For taxes, the state Appellate Tax Board guide says an abatement application is due by the first installment date on the bill, and assessors have three months to respond.

If you need a quick sale of a house with repairs, tenants or an estate, we purchase as is, and you can compare our offer with a listing. Ask the Fitchburg assessors for your bill dates and the Northern Worcester registry about recording.

faqs.a: Fitchburg is in Worcester County, Massachusetts, and is the county's third-largest city.
Wikipedia says Fitchburg hosts the Northern Worcester County Registry of Deeds, established in 1903. Confirm hours and recording steps with the registry.

faqs.q: How many people live in Fitchburg?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 41,946 residents, and the Census Bureau estimate for July 2025 is 42,136.

faqs.q: Do I need a smoke and CO certificate to sell in Fitchburg?
faqs.a: Yes. Massachusetts requires a certificate of compliance from the local fire department for a sale, and the department charges a fee.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Fitchburg house that needs a new roof or heating?
faqs.a: Yes. You can sell as is to a cash buyer, or repair and list it. Compare the repair costs and time against an offer.
